title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page in the divided-power de Rham dossier (cote 136), placed between typed pages of other exposés. It works out a duality between a polynomial algebra and a divided-power algebra, and asks whether a truncated extension-of-scalars functor is fully faithful.

(1) Set-up. S = k[U] is graded with U^n = U_n in degree -n. The dual S^∨ (written S^h in the transcription) is k{{T}}, a completed divided-power algebra. The note 'à faire en S-modules (gradués) avec S = k{T}' suggests recasting everything as graded modules over the divided-power algebra k{T} = Γ_k(T). The element T^{(k)} acts on S by contraction, U_{n+k} ↦ c_{n,k} U_n with c_{n,k} = binom(n+k, k), i.e. by the Hasse–Schmidt operators ∂^k/k!.

(2) The functor. Extension of scalars gives i_*: Mod(k) → Mod gr. k{T} = 𝓜, M ↦ M⊗_k S.

(3) Truncation. Grothendieck introduces the 'cotronqué' (stupid) truncation σ_N(P) = P/τ_{N+1}(P), so σ_N(P)_i = P_i for i ≤ N and 0 otherwise. This is a 'longue à gauche' truncation in degree N. He considers σ_N ∘ i_* for N ≤ 0 and then lets N → -∞, i.e. a pro-object P_∞.

(4) Claimed theorem: the truncated functor σ_N i_* (written τ_N i_*) is fully faithful.

(5) Attempted proof by adjunction: Hom_𝓜(M⊗S, N) = Hom_k(M, Hom_𝓜(S, N)). This reduces the claim to whether Hom_𝓜(S, τ^N(N⊗S)) ≃ N_0; he marks this with '??'. In parallel he tries a dual description: V(S) is the dual module, V_S(M) = V(M⊗S) = (k' ↦ Hom_k(M, S^{k'})), and Hom of V(S)-modules, with continuous Hom ('t-Hom_cont').

(6) Explicit computation. A k{T}-linear map S → M⊗S sends U_n to η_n = ξ_n U_n with ξ_n ∈ M. Linearity forces T^{(k)} η_{n+k} = c_{n,k} η_n, i.e. c_{n,k}(ξ_{n+k} - ξ_n) = 0.

(7) What the computation shows.
- Untruncated: c_{0,k} = 1, so every ξ_k equals ξ_0 and Hom = M in any characteristic.
- Truncated: degrees 0 … |N|-1 are removed, so the chain back to ξ_0 is lost. In characteristic p the binomials can vanish (e.g. binom(p, p-1) = 0), so the ξ_n need not all agree. The truncated statement can then fail, which explains the '??' and the passage to the pro-limit N → -∞.

Purpose: a technical lemma on the duality between the polynomial and divided-power algebras, i.e. Cartier duality between the formal additive group and its PD dual. This is the linear algebra underlying the PD de Rham complex.
errors: The full-faithfulness claim for the truncated functor σ_N i_* (fixed N < 0) appears doubtful in characteristic p. The constraints c_{n,k}(ξ_{n+k} - ξ_n) = 0 with c_{n,k} = binom(n+k, k) do not force all ξ_n to be equal once the low degrees are cut off. Grothendieck's own '??' signals this; the statement presumably holds only in characteristic 0, or after passing to the pro-system N → -∞.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine scratch computation on polynomial/divided-power duality and a truncation lemma. It is mildly interesting as a trace of the characteristic-p subtlety (vanishing binomials), but nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'S^h = k{{T}}' is likely 'S^∨ = k{{T}}' (the dual of S).
'"longueur à gauche"' should read '"longue à gauche"'.
The theorem line likely concerns σ_N i_* (as in the preceding line), written τ_N i_*; 'pl. fid.' = pleinement fidèle.
The 'D' before V_S(M) is crossed out, not part of the formula.
